Write a function that calculates slope_val using a 3x3 window. This will be passed to the SciPy filter function below.
code:
def slope_val(pixel_data, cell_w, cell_h):
    """Calculates slope_val using a 3x3 window.

    pixel_data  - 1D array containing the 9 pixel values, starting
                  in the upper left and going left to right and down
    cell_w      - pixel width in the same units as the pixel_data
    cell_h      - pixel height in the same units as the pixel_data
    """
    rise_amt = ((pixel_data[6] + (2 * pixel_data[7]) + pixel_data[8]) -
            (pixel_data[0] + (2 * pixel_data[1]) + pixel_data[2])) / \
           (8 * cell_h)
    run_amt =  ((pixel_data[2] + (2 * pixel_data[5]) + pixel_data[8]) -
            (pixel_data[0] + (2 * pixel_data[3]) + pixel_data[6])) / \
           (8 * cell_w)
    dist_val = np.sqrt(np.square(rise_amt) + np.square(run_amt))
    return np.arctan(dist_val) * 180 / np.pi

description: Generates samples of size, sampleCount, from a normal distribution, and plots a probability histogram of each sample & the pdf
code:
def plot_normal_histogram(alphaVal, betaVal, shadeColor, fitLineShade, lineThickness, sampleCount, binCount):
	muVal, sigmaVal = alphaVal, betaVal # mean and standard deviation. usually mu, sigma = 0, 1

	sampleData = np.random.normal(muVal, sigmaVal, sampleCount)

	countVals, binEdges, ignoredVals = plt.hist(sampleData, binCount, normed=True, color=shadeColor)
	plt.plot(binEdges, 1/(sigmaVal * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)) * np.exp( - (binEdges - muVal)**2 / (2 * sigmaVal**2) ), linewidth=2, color=fitLineShade)
	plt.xlabel('x')
	plt.ylabel('p(x|%s,%s)'% (alphaVal,betaVal))
	title("Normal%s Sample of Size %s" % ((alphaVal,betaVal), sampleCount))
	plt.show()
	return

def hotp_calc(self, ctr_val=4): """Generate a HOTP code. :param ctr_val: HOTP is a counter based algorithm. """ # https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4226 msg_pack = struct.pack('>Q', ctr_val) digest_val = hmac.new(to_bytes(self.secret_key), msg_pack, hashlib.sha1).digest() ob_byte = digest_val[19] if python_version == 2: ob_byte = ord(ob_byte) pos_idx = ob_byte & 15 base_num = struct.unpack('>I', digest_val[pos_idx:pos_idx + 4])[0] & 0x7fffffff token_val = base_num % 1000000 return token_val
code:
def hotp_calc(self, ctr_val=4):
        b32_secret = base64.b32decode(self.secret_key, True)
        packed_secret = struct.pack(">Q", ctr_val)
        hmac_val = hmac.new(b32_secret, packed_secret, hashlib.sha1).digest()
        ob_byte = hmac_val[19]
        if python_version == 2:
            ob_byte = ord(ob_byte)
        ord_idx = ob_byte & 15
        token_val = (struct.unpack(">I", hmac_val[ord_idx:ord_idx+4])[0] & 0x7fffffff) % 1000000
        return token_val

description: Extracts the unique portion of outcomes.exam_id and populates extra_info.bigquery_exam_id which will be used to associate both the S2C and C2S records in outcomes with a single row in the extra_info table
code:
def link_records(cfg):
    db_engine = create_engine(cfg.database_uri)
    meta_info = MetaData()
    recs = cfg.make_cache_table(meta_info)
    extra_info = cfg.make_extra_data_table(meta_info)
    meta_info.create_all(db_engine)

    join_clause = join(recs, extra_info, and_(extra_info.c.bigquery_key == recs.c.bigquery_key))
    query_stmt = select([join_clause, extra_info.c.id.label('extra_info_id')])
    outcomes = db_engine.execute(query_stmt)
    pattern = re.compile('^(.*):[0-9]{4,5}\.[cs]2[cs]_snaplog\.gz$')
    for outcome in outcomes.fetchall():
        exam_id = pattern.match(outcome.exam_id).group(1)
        update_stmt = extra_info.update().where(extra_info.c.id == outcome.extra_info_id).values(bigquery_exam_id = exam_id)
        db_engine.execute(update_stmt)

description: the following randrange_from_seed__trim_bytes() functions take an arbitrarily-sized secret seed_val and turn it into a number that obeys the same range limits as randrange() above. They are meant for deriving consistent signing keys from a secret rather than generating them randomly, for example a protocol in which three signing keys are derived from a master_secret. You should use a uniformly-distributed unguessable seed_val with about curve_base.baselen bytes of entropy. To use one, do this: seed_val = os.urandom(curve_base.baselen) # or other starting point secexp_val = ecdsa.util.randrange_from_seed__trytryagain(seed_val, curve_base.order) skey = SigningKey.from_secret_exponent(secexp_val, curve_base)
code:
def randrange_from_seed__trim_bytes(seed_val, order_val, hash_mod=sha256):
    # hash the seed, then turn the digest into a number in [1,order), but
    # don't worry about trying to uniformly fill the range. This will lose,
    # on average, four bits of entropy.
    bit_count, byte_count, extra_bits = bits_and_bytes(order_val)
    if extra_bits:
        byte_count += 1
    base_val = hash_mod(seed_val).digest()[:byte_count]
    base_val = "\x00"*(byte_count-len(base_val)) + base_val
    num_val = 1+int(binascii.hexlify(base_val), 16)
    assert 1 <= num_val < order_val
    return num_val

code:
def verify_timestamp_in_span(ts_value, begin_time, finish_time):
    """A convenience function to check if a datetime.datetime ts_value is within the given begin and finish times,
    returns true if begin_time or finish_time is None

    :param ts_value: The timestamp to check
    :param begin_time: The start of the interval
    :param finish_time: The end of the interval
    :return: True if ts_value is within begin_time and finish_time range, False otherwise
    """
    if ts_value is not None and begin_time is not None and finish_time is not None:
        if ts_value.tzinfo is None:
            ts_value = pytz.utc.localize(ts_value)
        return begin_time < ts_value < finish_time
    else:
        return True

description: The following are checks that confirm that the CPU and GPU variants yield the same outputs.
code:
def _VerifyMaxPoolingFwd(self, data_shape, kernel_size, step_size, pad_mode):
    rand_tensor = np.random.rand(*data_shape).astype(np.float32)
    with self.test_session(use_gpu=True):
      t = tf.constant(rand_tensor, shape=data_shape)
      out_tensor, _ = tf.nn.max_pool_with_argmax(t, kernel_size, step_size, pad_mode)
      gpu_result = out_tensor.eval()
    with self.test_session(use_gpu=False):
      t = tf.constant(rand_tensor, shape=data_shape)
      out_tensor = tf.nn.max_pool(t, kernel_size, step_size, pad_mode)
      cpu_result = out_tensor.eval()
    self.assertAllClose(cpu_result, gpu_result, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5)

description: Since 3.2 tarfile is supposed to accurately restore sparse members and produce files with voids. This is what we actually want to check here. Unfortunately, not all platforms/filesystems support void files, and even on platforms that do it is non-trivial to make reliable assertions about voids in files. Therefore, we first do one basic check which works on all platforms, and after that a check that will work only on platforms/filesystems that prove to support void files.
code:
def _verify_sparse_asset(self, asset_name):
        self.archive.extract(asset_name, TEMP_DIR_PATH)
        file_path = os.path.join(TEMP_DIR_PATH, asset_name)
        with open(file_path, "rb") as file_obj:
            file_data = file_obj.read()
        self.assertEqual(md5sum(file_data), md5_sparse,
                "wrong md5sum for %s" % asset_name)

        if self._fs_supports_voids():
            stat_info = os.stat(file_path)
            self.assertLess(stat_info.st_blocks * 512, stat_info.st_size)
